column3: Oscillatory neural networks and oscillator computing hardware (VO2, spin-torque/spin-Hall nano-oscillators, CMOS ring and relaxation oscillators, ReRAM-coupled, MEMS, photonic). Cover device mismatch, frequency dispersion, phase noise, coupling variability, calibration. Seeds to verify: arXiv 2211.05497 (DONN mismatch), npj Unconventional Computing s44335-024-00015-z.

Kuramoto and learned-oscillator ML models (AKOrN artificial Kuramoto oscillatory neurons, Kuramoto orientation diffusion, equilibrium propagation on oscillators, OscNet, oscillator Hopfield/associative memory, Un-0 by Unconventional AI) and any robustness or perturbation analysis of them. Seeds to verify: arXiv 2504.11884 (EqProp Kuramoto), arXiv 2503.16183.

Oscillator-based Ising machines and coherent Ising machines: noise, variability, noise-as-resource, and how robustness is reported and mitigated at scale (number of spins, success probability, mismatch tolerance).

Analog in-memory computing non-idealities and hardware-aware / noise-injection training (IBM AIHWKit, PCM/RRAM drift and programming noise, variance-aware training, drift compensation, global calibration), including what does NOT work. Seeds to verify: Nature Communications 2023 s41467-023-40770-4 (HWA training), arXiv 2102.06365, arXiv 1808.08412.

Generative models on noisy/analog/physical hardware: diffusion on compute-in-memory (EtaMix at DATE 2026, ASSERT, guidance recalibration), analog diffusion models, optical generative models, resistive-memory score-based solvers, thermodynamic/probabilistic computing (Extropic, Normal Computing), physical generative models. Seeds to verify: arXiv 2609.00955 (ASSERT), arXiv 2608.19644, arXiv 2404.05648.

Error correction and redundancy for analog computation: Ron Roth's analog error-correcting codes and follow-ups, algorithm-based fault tolerance, redundancy / multiple devices per weight, ensemble or layer averaging, TMR analogues for analog, coded computation, and ESPECIALLY phase / circular-mean averaging or redundancy in oscillator systems (search hard for this: e.g. averaging redundant oscillator copies, phase-domain voting, synchronization of redundant oscillator arrays to reduce phase noise such as N-coupled-oscillator phase noise reduction ~1/N, circular statistics in neuromorphic readout). Seeds to verify: Roth analog ECC papers, arXiv 2402.13503, Pedretti et al. redundancy and bit slicing IEEE TED Parts I/II, arXiv 2404.15621.

Physical neural networks and in-situ / physics-aware / digital-twin training (Wright & McMahon et al. Nature 2022 physics-aware training), the sim-to-real gap, chip-in-the-loop calibration. Also mixed-signal neuromorphic mismatch (BrainScaleS, DYNAP-SE, analog Loihi-like) and how they calibrate.

Robustness of neural ODEs and continuous-time / reservoir systems to parameter perturbation and stochastic (SDE) noise: noise as regularisation (neural SDEs), sensitivity / Lyapunov analysis, physical reservoir computing under noise, robustness of implicit / equilibrium models (DEQs), and robustness of ODE/flow-based samplers to discretisation and parameter noise.

Fault and yield modelling for analog/AI accelerators: Monte Carlo process-variation yield, stuck-at faults and dead units, aging/drift, ADC/readout noise and quantisation, fault-tolerant DNN methods (fault-aware training, remapping onto spares, dropout-style), and the metrics used to report yield.

Everything Unconventional AI (unconv.ai, Naveen Rao) has published or said: the Un-0 paper/report/blog and GitHub repo unconv-ai/Un-0, talks, interviews, patents, job posts touching hardware non-idealities, variability, noise robustness. Same for peer startups (Extropic, Normal Computing, Lightmatter, Mythic, EnCharge AI, Sagence, Rain AI, etc.) on robustness / non-idealities / calibration.
